sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 7 seeking to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.8677 of 2022 on the file of learned I Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-XII Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Medchal-Malkajgiri District at Kukatpally, registered for the offences under Sections 420, 468, 471, 384, 447 and 506 read with 34 I.P.C.
2.

entities.text: Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-XII Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Medchal-Malkajgiri District at Kukatpally
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Pilli Nagaraj, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri E. Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for 2 ETD,J respondent No.1-State and Sri D. Bhaskar Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that accused Nos.1 to 7 with a common intention to cheat LW.1 (de facto complainant) and to grab the land in Plot No.13 in Survey Nos.156, 157 to 162, 175, 176 and 177/A situated at Suraram Village, Quthubullahpur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, have created certain documents illegally, by suppressing the death of the original owner Jonnada Venkatesham,
knowing fully-well that the documents are not valid, and that accused No.1, claiming himself as owner of the said plot, executed Sale Deeds in favour of different parties.

It is alleged that,
subsequently, accused Nos.2 to 7 have trespassed into the subject plot of LW.1, damaged the structures and threatened LW.1 with dire consequences.
Further, the accused have extorted LW.1 to handover the title deed of Plot No.13 bearing document No.226/1969 to them.

Thus, the present case is registered for the offences under Sections 420, 468, 471, 384, 447 and 506 read with 34 I.P.C.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the civil matter is given a criminal colour just to harass the petitioners.
He 3 ETD,J further submitted that the de facto complainant does not hold any document to prove that Plot No.13 belongs to him.

He further submitted that the case is wrongly registered by the Kukatpally police, while it has to be registered by Dundigal police, since the subject property is located within the limits of Dundigal police.

He further submitted that there are two F.I.Rs. registered with similar set of allegations and thus, it amounts to double jeopardy and hence,
the proceedings in the present C.C. are liable to be quashed by applying the principle laid down by the Honourable Apex Court in T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala and others 1, wherein it was held that in respect of the same cognizable offence and same occurrence when two F.I.Rs. had been lodged,
there can be no second F.I.R. and no fresh investigation on receipt of every subsequent information in respect of the same cognizable offence or same occurrence giving rise to one or more cognizable offences.

entities.text: T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala and others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He, therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings in the present C.C. against the petitioners herein.
5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted that respondent No.2-de facto complainant is a bona fide purchaser of the subject property from LW.5.

He further submitted that one (2001) 6 SCC 181 4 ETD,J Jonnada Venkatesham has executed GPA in favour of petitioner No.1-accused No.1 vide document No.68 of 1992, dated 05.02.1992, and the said Jonnada Venkatesham died on 27.10.1996.

He further submitted that petitioner No.1-accused No.1 on noticing that all the plots were not occupied by the owners, who purchased them, planned to grab 36 plots which were in the original layout of Jonnada Venkatesham, without there being any legal right and he used his GPA illegally, claimed possession over the said plots and fraudulently executed Sale Deeds in favour of third parties.
He further submitted that accused No.1 fraudulently executed Sale Deeds in favour of petitioner Nos.2, 4, 6 and 7.
Further, petitioner No.2-accused No.2 has gifted the property to petitioner No.3-accused No.3.
Since the title of petitioner No.2-accused No.2 itself is defective, she cannot gift any property to petitioner No.3-accused No.3.

He further submitted that since the accused have resorted to creation of false and fabricated documents, criminal element is involved in the alleged acts and thus, criminal case is very much maintainable.
He, therefore, prayed to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

The learned counsel has relied upon the judgment of the 5 ETD,J Honourable Apex Court in Nagpur Steel and Alloys Private Limited v. P. Radhakrishna Alias Rajan and others 2.
6.

entities.text: Nagpur Steel and Alloys Private Limited v. P. Radhakrishna Alias Rajan and others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Perused the record.

7. The allegations in the complaint point out that the petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 7 have resorted to creating false and fabricated documents and have registered the plots in favour of third parties,
without there being any right conveyed to petitioner No.1-accused No.1.
The contention of the petitioners' counsel is that there are two F.I.Rs. registered with similar set of allegations and thus, it amounts to double jeopardy.
As seen from the charge sheet, the first F.I.R. is registered on the complaint lodged by petitioner No.4-accused No.4, but the petitioners have not placed any such complaint on record.

However, learned counsel for respondent No.2 has brought to the notice of this Court that the first F.I.R. was registered based on the complaint given by petitioner No.4-accused No.4 based on a different incident and that the de facto complainant has lodged only one complaint.
Therefore, the principle laid down in T.T. Antony's case (supra 1) does not get attracted to the present case.

The other contention 1997 SCC (Cri) 1073 6 ETD,J raised by the petitioners' counsel is P.Jayaprakash Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187151162/
2 that the police, who do not have jurisdiction have investigated the matter and that the case is pending in the wrong Court.

sentences.text: However, it is borne out by record that the case has been subsequently transferred from the Court at Kukatpally to the Court of Medchal-Malkajgiri.
Apart from the de facto complainant and LW.2, LWs.3 and 4 are the officials representing the Banks, which have given loans on the subject property.
LWs.5 and 6 are listed as witnesses.
Thus, the evidence of all these witnesses needs to be tested during the course of trial.

8. In Nagpur Steel and Alloys Private Limited's case (supra 2), it is held that:
"3. We have perused the complaint carefully.

entities.text: Nagpur Steel and Alloys Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In our opinion it cannot be said that the complaint did not disclose the commission of an offence.
Merely because the offence was committed during the course of a commercial transaction, would not be sufficient to hold that the complaint did not warrant a trial.
Whether or not the allegations in the complaint were true was to be decided on the basis of evidence to be led at the trial in the complaint case.
It certainly was not a case in which the criminal trial should have been cut short.
The quashing of the complaint has resulted in grave miscarriage of justice.
We, therefore, without expressing 7 ETD,J any opinion on the merits of the case, allow this appeal and set aside the impugned order of the High Court and restore the complaint.
The learned trial Magistrate shall proceed with the complaint and dispose of it in accordance with law expeditiously."
9. In the present case, the allegations point out a prima facie case against the petitioners.

In view of the above held discussion and by applying the principle laid down in Nagpur Steel and Alloys Private Limited's case (supra 2), it is opined that it is not a fit case to quash the proceedings in the present C.C.

entities.text: Nagpur Steel and Alloys Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: However, it is deemed appropriate to dispense with the attendance of the petitioners before the trial Court.

10. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of dispensing with the attendance of the petitioners before the trial Court provided they are represented by a counsel before the trial Court on every date of hearing and shall appear before the trial Court whenever their presence is required during the course of trial.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

__ JUSTICE TIRUMALA DEVI EADA Date: 06.03.2026.
